name: The Rusty Nail
look: A dingy bar that smells like stale beer and broken promises. Rain ticks the front windows. Thunder mutters over the river, still a long way off. Sal the bartender is behind the counter. Earl, an old regular, is on a stool. A scarred wooden bar runs down the left wall. Wobbly tables crowd the right. An old jukebox glows in the corner. Two doorways wait in the back: one marked GENTS, one propped open on the alley.

exits.blockedText: It's even hotter out there. You've come too far to turn back now.

hotspots.look: A door marked GENTS. The paint is losing.
Propped open. The alley breathes hot rain at you.
A 1960s Seeburg full of old 45s. A hand-written sign: "$1 BILLS ONLY. NO SINGLES SMALLER THAN A DOLLAR, WISE GUY."
Decades of wood, rings, and initials. Somebody carved SAL WAS HERE. Sal is still here.
Bottles, a spotted mirror, and taps that have pulled a lot of bad decisions.
Sticky. One holds Earl's empty glass, spiritually. The near table is close enough to walk behind.
A flickering sign reads RUSTY NAIL. The N is out. Charlie doesn't care.
Two lamps that have given up on being bright.
The street is hotter than the bar, which is saying something.
Tattooed forearms, an anchor and a heart that reads MA. A towel rides his shoulder. He looks like change is a personal insult.
An old regular nursing a glass that has already given up.
Rain ticks the glass, a few drops at a time. Thunder rolls somewhere over the river. Close enough to feel. Not close enough to help.
An empty pickle jar labelled TIPS — KARMA IS REAL.
